department: Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India
benefit: If you live in a village and have no house or a kutcha house, you get money to build a pucca house of at least 25 square metres. In plain areas like Tamil Nadu you get Rs 1,20,000, paid into your bank account in parts. You also get up to 95 days of MGNREGS work wages and Rs 12,000 for a toilet. You can take an optional bank loan of up to Rs 70,000.

other: For rural families with no house, or living in a kutcha house.
Families are chosen from the SECC 2011 and AwaasPlus survey lists, checked at the Gram Sabha.
Priority for houseless families, SC/ST families, primitive tribal groups and women-headed families.

how_to_apply: You cannot apply on your own. Families are picked from survey lists and checked at the Gram Sabha. You can check your status on the PMAY-G website. If your name is left out wrongly, you can appeal to the Block Development Officer (BDO) or file a complaint on CPGRAMS.
where_to_apply: Gram Sabha and Block Development Officer (BDO); status check on pmayg.dord.gov.in

evidence.quote: PMAY-G provides financial grants directly to rural homeless families and those living in kutcha dwellings
Minimum House Size: 25 square metres, including a dedicated kitchen area.
Financial Grant (Plain Areas): ₹ 1,20,000 per house, delivered directly via bank transfer.
Up to 95 person-days of daily wage employment under MGNREGS
optional low-interest bank loans up to ₹ 70,000 for house enlargement
eligible families are identified based on housing deprivation and kutcha home criteria from the official SECC 2011 and updated AwaasPlus surveys
Every draft list is read aloud and publicly validated at the local Gram Sabha village assembly.
